blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, AI use cases are managed like investments — a small portfolio, deliberately balanced between safe bets, productive workhorses, and one or two genuinely exploratory projects. Too much safety and the portfolio never learns anything new. Too much exploration and nothing ever reaches production.

The best executives I have worked with keep a simple ratio in mind. Roughly 70% of AI effort goes on proven, steady workhorses that deliver boring but reliable value. Roughly 20% goes on projects that extend what the team already understands — one step into the unknown. Roughly 10% goes on genuine experiments that will either open a new direction or teach an expensive lesson. Neither outcome is bad; both are useful.

Had we kept the portfolio all in the '10% experiments' bucket, we would have had an exciting year and nothing to show for it. Balance is the whole point — and balance is boring exactly because it works.

items.q: How does the author suggest AI use cases should be managed?
options: As a fixed annual budget line
items.why: "AI use cases are managed like investments — a small portfolio".

items.q: According to the text, what does the roughly 70% share of effort go on?
options: Proven, steady workhorses that deliver reliable value
items.why: "70% of AI effort goes on proven, steady workhorses that deliver boring but reliable value."

items.q: What does the author say about the two possible outcomes of the 10% experiments?
options: Both are useful, whether they succeed or fail
An expensive lesson is a wasted year
items.why: "either open a new direction or teach an expensive lesson. Neither outcome is bad; both are useful."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A portfolio needs both proven work and exploration.
A balanced ratio helps the portfolio keep learning.
Putting everything into experiments is the boldest and best strategy.
Reliable value can look unexciting yet still matter.
items.why: Inferência: o autor diz que tudo em experimentos daria "an exciting year and nothing to show for it" — ele critica exatamente essa aposta.

items.q: The final line — "balance is boring exactly because it works" — suggests that the author believes…
options: the appeal of a plan is a poor guide to its value
balance is a temporary phase before scaling up
excitement is a reliable sign of good strategy
boring projects should eventually be dropped
items.why: Inferência: o que empolga não é o que entrega; o que vale é justamente o discreto e constante.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James apresentando o portfólio ao conselho. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
I know some of you came in today expecting a moonshot — one bold, headline-grabbing AI bet. What I am going to show you instead is a portfolio, and I would ask you to hear me out before you decide it is too modest.

Seventy percent of our effort sits on workhorses. Forecasting, document handling, contract screening — unglamorous, but they pay for themselves every quarter. Twenty percent extends what we already do well, one careful step into the unknown. And ten percent — only ten — is reserved for genuine experiments, the ones that might open a new direction or teach us an expensive lesson.

Now, had we put everything into that ten percent, we would have walked in here with a thrilling story and no results. I have watched teams do precisely that. The demo dazzles the board, and eighteen months later nothing has reached production.

So my recommendation is balance. It will not make headlines. But it will compound, quietly, year after year — and that, I would argue, is exactly what this business needs from AI.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What had some board members been expecting before James spoke?
options: A decision to pause AI investment
A report on last year's failures
A cost-cutting plan for the AI team
items.why: "some of you came in today expecting a moonshot — one bold, headline-grabbing AI bet."

items.q: Which examples does James give of the 70% workhorses?
options: Forecasting, document handling and contract screening
items.why: "Forecasting, document handling, contract screening — unglamorous, but they pay for themselves."

items.q: What does James say happens when teams put everything into experiments?
options: They dazzle the board but reach nothing after eighteen months
They reach production faster than expected
They run out of budget within a quarter
They lose the board's attention immediately
items.why: "The demo dazzles the board, and eighteen months later nothing has reached production."

items.q: When James says the balanced plan "will not make headlines. But it will compound, quietly," he is implying that…
options: the board should not be told about the plan
quiet, steady gains ultimately outweigh a dramatic story
headlines are the true measure of AI success
the plan will take too long to show any value
items.why: Inferência: ele contrapõe manchete a acúmulo constante, defendendo o segundo como o que realmente entrega.

items.q: How would you best describe James's stance toward the board?
options: Confident, persuading them that balance beats spectacle
Apologetic about offering a modest plan
Frustrated with their appetite for risk
items.why: Inferência: ele pede que o ouçam, antecipa a objeção e argumenta com firmeza a favor do equilíbrio.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We manage our AI initiatives as a single portfolio, not a list of pet projects." A portfolio is…
options: a collection of holdings managed together
items.why: Portfolio = conjunto de iniciativas geridas em bloco, com balanceamento entre elas.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Automated invoice matching is our reliable ___ — dull, but it earns its keep every month."
items.why: Workhorse = cavalo de tração: o projeto sem glamour que entrega valor de forma constante.

items.q: "The 70-20-10 split is really about the ratio between them." A ratio is…
options: the proportional relationship between the parts
items.why: Ratio = proporção, a relação relativa entre as fatias do portfólio.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Contract screening delivers ___, unglamorous value — the same result quarter after quarter."
items.why: Steady = constante, previsível — o oposto do experimento arriscado.

items.q: "A failed pilot need not be a loss; often it is simply an expensive lesson." This phrase describes…
options: a costly mistake that still teaches something valuable
a budget overrun with no benefit at all
a training course paid for by the company
a fee charged by an external consultant
items.why: Expensive lesson = lição cara: custa, mas o aprendizado tem valor.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões sobre estratégia de IA. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the 70-20-10 split." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the forecasting model desk by desk over the quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on spending anything on experiments." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team loved the demo but never followed through to production." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "A flashy moonshot demo rarely moves the needle on real results." This means it…
options: does not make a noticeable difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
